# Introduction

This document contains code and supporting information accompanying the manuscript "A test for linkage disequilibrium in structured populations." We organize the document by figure in order of appearance in the main text. 

Some time-consuming chunks below are set not to run by default. Instead, we ran these code chunks on the ARGO SLURM cluster (managed by the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics at Princeton University) and provide intermediate $\texttt{.rds}$ files in the $\texttt{rdata}$ directory to be loaded inside of plotting chunks. This directory contains sub-directories corresponding to each of the human studies we analyze in this study ($\texttt{TGP\_rdata}$, $\texttt{HGDP\_rdata}$, $\texttt{HO\_rdata}$), as well as a sub-directory for simulation studies ($\texttt{power\_sim}$). The $\texttt{figures}$ directory in turn contains the output figures. 

# Libraries
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2) # main plotting library
library(ggh4x) # additional plotting utilities 
library(dplyr) # for working with dataframes
library(latex2exp) # LaTeX labels/headings in plots
library(patchwork) # arrange subplots in figure
library(bnpsd) # simulate structured genotypes
library(alstructure) # estimate IAFs
library(qvalue) # for statistical power simulations
library(biomaRt) # BioMart database for SNP attributes
source("./structLD/R/sLD_SNP.R")
source("./structLD/R/compute_p_val.R")
source("./structLD/R/compute_entropy.R")
```

# Datasets

Our analyses center on three human studies: the Thousand Genomes Project (TGP) [@tgp2015], Human Genome Diversity Project (HGDP) [@cavalli-sforza2005], and Human Origins (HO) study [@lazaridis2014]. We process the datasets in the same manner as was done in [@hao2019]. In brief, we filter out closely related individuals and genotypes with an allele frequency below $0.05$ for each dataset, with some additional filtering on genotype completeness. Our resulting genotype matrices have the following dimensions:

* TGP: $1815$ individuals and $1229310$ SNPs.
* HGDP: $940$ individuals and $550303$ SNPs.
* HO: $2251$ individuals and $372446$ SNPs.

The [datasets](https://github.com/StoreyLab/alstructure_paper/tree/master/data) analyzed in this study can be found in the Storey Lab repository for the $\texttt{alstructure}$ manuscript [@cabreros2019].

# Main Figures
## Figure 1 {#sec-fig1}

In this figure, we apply the sLD test to pairs of loci residing on different chromosomes using the TGP dataset. We show histograms corresponding to three different models of population structure: an unstructured model, a model partially accounting for structure, and a model capturing most of the structure in the population. 

### Sample SNPs across distinct chromosomes 

Our goal is to evaluate interchromosomal LD for different models of population structure. As such, we randomly draw a large number of locus pairs ($2 \times 10^6$) spanning different chromosomes. The following code chunks produce a file named $\texttt{TGP\_diff\_chr\_ids.rds}$, containing pairs of indices corresponding to SNPs on distinct chromosomes within the TGP dataset; these indices are consistent with the ordering of SNPs in the file $\texttt{TGP.bed}$. We keep this file in the directory $\texttt{./rdata/TGP\_rdata/diff\_chr}$. We use the BioMart database to obtain information about SNPs (i.e., chromosome number, base pair coordinate) [@smedley2009]. Note that we end with $1229022$ unique annotated SNPs after this step (out of the original $1229310$). 

The directory $\texttt{./data/TGP}$ below is a placeholder for the user's path to the raw data files and should be replaced accordingly. Each human dataset is in PLINK format [@purcell2007] and consists of a set of three files (ending with the extensions $\texttt{.bed}$, $\texttt{.bim}$, and $\texttt{.fam}$). 

```{r, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
# Load TGP SNP IDs
TGP <- BEDMatrix::BEDMatrix("./data/TGP/TGP", simple_names = TRUE)
rsid_TGP <- colnames(TGP)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Get SNP information from BioMart database 
snp_mart <- biomaRt::useMart(
  biomart = "ENSEMBL_MART_SNP", 
  dataset = "hsapiens_snp", 
  host = "https://e116.ensembl.org" 
)

results_tgp <- biomaRt::getBM(
  attributes = c("refsnp_id", "chr_name", "chrom_start", "allele"),
  filters = "snp_filter",
  values = rsid_TGP,
  mart = snp_mart
)

snp_info_TGP <- results_tgp[!duplicated(results_tgp$refsnp_id), ] # remove duplicates, if any
saveRDS(snp_info_TGP, "./rdata/TGP_rdata/snp_info_TGP.rds")
```

We include a helper function below named $\texttt{sample\_across\_chromosomes()}$ that enables us to randomly sample pairs of loci spanning different chromosomes. We use this function here for the TGP, and call it later for the HGDP and HO datasets. We also add a simple function $\texttt{match\_rsid\_index()}$ that allows us to identify the index of a given SNP in the original PLINK genotype dataset.  

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Function for sampling locus pairs spanning two different chromosomes 
sample_across_chromosomes <- function(snp_info, n_pairs) {
  snps_by_chr <- split(snp_info$refsnp_id, snp_info$chr_name)
  chr_names <- as.character(1:22)
  pair_rsid <- matrix(nrow = n_pairs, ncol = 2)
  
  for (i in 1:n_pairs) {
    chr_pair <- sample(chr_names, 2, replace = FALSE)
    snp_a <- sample(snps_by_chr[[chr_pair[1]]], 1)
    snp_b <- sample(snps_by_chr[[chr_pair[2]]], 1)
    pair_rsid[i,] <- c(snp_a, snp_b)
  }
  
  return(pair_rsid)
}

match_rsid_index <- function(id_pairs, original_order) {
  locus_a_id <- match(id_pairs[,1], original_order)
  locus_b_id <- match(id_pairs[,2], original_order)
  
  return(cbind(locus_a_id, locus_b_id))
}
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
# Check number of annotated SNPs
snp_info_TGP <- readRDS("./rdata/TGP_rdata/snp_info_TGP.rds")
dim(snp_info_TGP)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Randomly draw interchromosomal locus pairs
set.seed(23)
pair_rsid <- sample_across_chromosomes(snp_info_TGP, 2e6)
TGP_diff_chr <- match_rsid_index(pair_rsid, rsid_TGP)
saveRDS(TGP_diff_chr, file = "./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_diff_chr_ids.rds")
```

### Perform sLD test on TGP data

We present a sample implementation below for performing the sLD test on the TGP dataset. The sLD test requires estimated individual-specific allele frequencies (IAFs) -- as detailed in the main text, we employ a semiparametric estimator of the admixture model, called $\texttt{alstructure}$ [@cabreros2019]. We truncate estimates to be in the range $[\tfrac{1}{2J}, 1 - \tfrac{1}{2J}]$, where $J$ is the number of individuals, as is done for the related structural Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (sHWE) test [@hao2019]; we do this to ensure that IAFs are not exactly equal to 0 or 1. In the example below, we model $K = 3$ admixed populations. 

Because it can be time-intensive to carry out the sLD test for a large number of locus pairs and/or a large range of admixed population counts $K$, we recommend parallelizing this analysis. We performed this analysis using ARGO, a SLURM cluster under the Lewis-
Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics at Princeton University. ARGO consists of a combination of AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon compute nodes. We include a function for cluster jobs below named $\texttt{sLD\_parallel()}$, which is compatible with multi-core processors. The argument $\texttt{cores}$ specifies the number of cores. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
sLD_parallel <- function(X, Pi, S, cores) {
  mclapply(1:nrow(S), function(i) {
    locus_a <- S[i, 1]
    locus_b <- S[i, 2]
    X_a <- X[locus_a, ]
    X_b <- X[locus_b, ]
    pi_a_vec <- Pi[locus_a, ]
    pi_b_vec <- Pi[locus_b, ]
    sLD_SNP(X_a, X_b, pi_a_vec, pi_b_vec)
  }, mc.cores = cores) |> unlist()
}

# Example usage:
# test_stat_vec <- sLD_parallel(X, Pi_hat, pair_indices, n_cores)
```


```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Convert BEDmatrix to R matrix 
X_TGP <- t(as.matrix(TGP)) # transpose to get loci x individuals format
X_TGP <- alstructure:::impute_mean(X_TGP) # impute missing values in genotype matrix

# Estimate IAFs
K <- 3 # choose the number of admixed populations
TGP_Pi_hat <- alstructure::estimate_F(X_TGP, d = K)$F_hat # estimated IAFs
TGP_test_stats_K3 <- numeric(2e6)

# Run sLD
TGP_diff_chr_ids <- readRDS("./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_diff_chr_ids.rds") # load_pair_indices
J_ind <- ncol(X_TGP) 
TGP_Pi_hat[TGP_Pi_hat < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind) # truncate IAF estimates 
TGP_Pi_hat[TGP_Pi_hat > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)
TGP_test_stats_K3 <- sLD(X_TGP, TGP_Pi_hat, TGP_diff_chr_ids)
saveRDS(TGP_test_stats_K3, file = "./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_K3_diff_chr.rds")
```

We also demonstrate how to estimate IAFs under an unstructured model (equivalent to $K=1$ admixed populations). Here, we can simply compute a single allele frequency for each locus, without using $\texttt{alstructure}$. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Estimate IAFs for an unstructured population model
TGP_Pi_hat <- matrix(rowMeans(X_TGP/2), nrow=nrow(X_TGP), ncol=ncol(X_TGP))
```

### Code for plotting 

We plot $p$-values for three different models of population structure. These are an unstructured model, partial structure model, and adequate structure model ($K=1$, $K=3$, and $K=19$ admixed populations, respectively). While we do not explicitly compute test statistics for $K=1$ and $K=19$ in this document, the code chunk above (which performs the sLD test with $K=3$ admixed populations) can be modified to use a different $K$. We also include a helper function below, named $\texttt{plot\_triple\_histograms()}$, that will be called throughout this document to create a plot consisting of three $p$-value histograms in a row. The intermediate files needed to plot this figure are contained in the directory $\texttt{rdata/TGP\_rdata}$. 

```{r}
# Function to generate subfigure
plot_triple_histograms <- function(plot_df, labels) {
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = p, y = after_stat(density))) + 
       geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0,
                      fill = "#CCD3DD", col = "black",
                      linewidth = 0.2) + 
       geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
       facet_wrap(~id, 
                  labeller = as_labeller(labels, default = label_parsed), 
                  scales = "free_y", 
                  ncol = 3) + 
       theme_bw(base_family = "sans") + 
       theme(text = element_text(size = 10),
             plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
             strip.background = element_blank(),
             strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "plain", 
                                       margin = margin(t = 2, r = 0, b = 2, l = 0)),
             panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5),
             panel.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines"),
             panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
             axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
             axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6),
             axis.text.y = element_blank(),
             axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
             aspect.ratio = 0.7
          ) + 
       labs(x = TeX(r"(\textit{p}-value)"), 
            y = "Density",
           )
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# Read in test stats and compute p-values
K_vec <- c(1,3,19)
p_vec <- c()
id_vec <- c()

for (i in K_vec) {
  obs_ts <- sprintf("./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_K%s_diff_chr.rds", i)
  obs_ts <- readRDS(obs_ts)
  p_K <- compute_p_val(obs_ts) # compute p-values from test stats
  p_vec <- c(p_vec, p_K)
  id_vec <- c(id_vec, rep(i, length(p_K)))
}

# Make dataframe for plotting
sLD_df_TGP <- data.frame(id = id_vec, p = p_vec)
sLD_df_TGP$id <- as.factor(sLD_df_TGP$id)
labels <- c(
  "1"  = "Unstructured~model~(italic(K)==1)",
  "3"  = "Partial~structure~model~(italic(K)==3)",
  "19" = "Adequate~structure~model~(italic(K)==19)"
)

p <- plot_triple_histograms(sLD_df_TGP, labels)

p
ggsave("./figures/figure1.png", plot = p, width = 6.5, height = 2, dpi = 600)
```

## Figure 3 {#sec-fig3}

Here, we simulate genotypes under an admixture model with $K=4$ admixed populations for $J = 800$ individuals at $I = 80000$ loci, using the $\texttt{bnpsd}$ library [@ochoa2021]. We draw ancestral allele frequencies from the $\text{Uniform}(0.05,0.95)$ distribution, admixed population allele frequencies via the Balding-Nichols distribution [@balding1995], and admixture proportions according to a Normal random walk along a one-dimensional geography [@ochoa2016]. We chose admixed population inbreeding coefficients of $0.1, 0.2, 0.3$ and $0.4$. IAFs are in turn estimated from the observed genotypes using $\texttt{alstructure}$ under the assumption that the true number of admixed populations is known (i.e., setting $K=4$) [@cabreros2019]. We filter out loci with a minor allele frequency below 0.01. 

### Simulate genotypes

```{r, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(42)
J_ind <- 800 # number of individuals
I_loci <- 80000 # number of loci
K_subpops <- 4 # number of admixed pops

# Draw admixture model parameters
inbr_subpops <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4) # admixed pop inbreeding coefficients
admix_proportions <- bnpsd::admix_prop_1d_linear(J_ind, K_subpops, sigma = 1)

# Draw IAFs 
p_anc <- bnpsd::draw_p_anc(I_loci, p_min = 0.05, p_max = 0.95)
p_subpops <- bnpsd::draw_p_subpops(p_anc, inbr_subpops)
p_ind <- bnpsd::make_p_ind_admix(p_subpops, admix_proportions)
p_ind[p_ind < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind) # truncate small/large IAFs
p_ind[p_ind > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)

# Draw genotypes, estimate IAFs
X <- bnpsd::draw_genotypes_admix(p_ind)
p_ind_marginal <- matrix(rowMeans(p_ind), 
                         nrow=nrow(p_ind), ncol=ncol(p_ind))
p_ind_hat <- alstructure::estimate_F(X, d = 4)$F_hat # assume K known 
p_ind_hat[p_ind_hat < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind) # truncate estimates
p_ind_hat[p_ind_hat > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)

# Filter out small MAFs (< 0.01)
min_MAF <- 0.01
maf_vec <- rowMeans(X, na.rm = TRUE) / 2
actual_maf <- pmin(maf_vec, 1 - maf_vec)
keep_rows <- which(actual_maf >= min_MAF)
X_filtered <- X[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE]
p_ind_filtered <- p_ind[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE]
p_ind_hat_filtered <- p_ind_hat[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE]
p_ind_marginal_filtered <- p_ind_marginal[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE]
```

### Perform sLD test on null pairs

We perform the sLD test on $50000$ randomly selected pairs of SNPs. We consider an unstructured population model (equivalent to $K=1$ admixed populations), the true population model, and an estimated population model. The corresponding test types will be referred to as traditional, sLD (theoretical), and sLD (implemented), respectively. Because we draw genotypes jointly independent of one another, these pairs represent true null hypotheses (no structural LD). Note that we can equivalently use the function $\texttt{sLD()}$ to compute test statistics. In this case, we would first compute a full set of locus pair indices, and input this set directly into $\texttt{sLD()}$. We explicitly loop over $\texttt{1:n\_pairs}$ here and use $\texttt{sLD\_SNP()}$ to demonstrate how individual test statistics are computed.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(41)
n_pairs <- 50000 # number of hypothesis tests
theor_vec <- numeric(n_pairs) # sLD test stat with true IAFs
imp_vec <- numeric(n_pairs) # sLD test stat with estimated IAFs
trad_vec <- numeric(n_pairs) # test assuming no structure 

for (i in 1:n_pairs) {
  loci_id <- sample(1:nrow(X_filtered), 2) # sample a pair of loci
  a_id <- loci_id[1]
  b_id <- loci_id[2]
  
  # Compute test statistics
  theor_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_filtered[a_id,], X_filtered[b_id,],
                          p_ind_filtered[a_id,], p_ind_filtered[b_id,])
  imp_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_filtered[a_id,], X_filtered[b_id,],
                        p_ind_hat_filtered[a_id,], p_ind_hat_filtered[b_id,])
  trad_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_filtered[a_id,], X_filtered[b_id,],
                         p_ind_marginal_filtered[a_id,],
                         p_ind_marginal_filtered[b_id,])
}

# Compute p-values from test stats
p_values_trad <- compute_p_val(trad_vec)
p_values_theor <- compute_p_val(theor_vec)
p_values_imp <- compute_p_val(imp_vec)

# Save output as .rds
saveRDS(
  list(trad = p_values_trad,
       theor  = p_values_theor,
       imp  = p_values_imp
      ),
  file = "./rdata/p_values_sim.rds",
)
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
theoretical <- -log10(ppoints(n))

               sort(-log10(p_values_theor), decreasing = TRUE),

                        color = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", 
              color = "darkgray") +
  geom_point(data = subset(qq_df, method == "Traditional"), 
             size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = subset(qq_df, method == "sLD (theoretical)"),

             size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_color_manual(breaks = c("Traditional", 
                                "sLD (theoretical)", 
                                "sLD (implemented)"),
                     values = c("Traditional" = "#E69F00", 
                                "sLD (theoretical)" = "#56B4E9", 
                                "sLD (implemented)" = "#009E73")) +
  scale_shape_manual(breaks = c("Traditional", 
                                "sLD (theoretical)", 
                                "sLD (implemented)"),
                     values = c("Traditional" = 16, 
                                "sLD (theoretical)" = 17, 
                                "sLD (implemented)" = 15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(qq_df$expected)), ylim = c(0, 10)) + 
  labs(x = TeX(r"(Theoretical -log$_{10}$(Uniform(0,1) quantiles))"),
       y = TeX(r"(Observed -log$_{10}$(\textit{p}-values))"),
       color = "Method", shape = "Method") + 
  theme_bw(base_family = "sans") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, 
                                    linewidth = 0.5),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1)),
         shape = guide_legend())

# Assemble layout
layout <- "
  ##AABB##
  ###CC###
"

p <- (pA | pB) / (plot_spacer() + pC + 
                    plot_spacer() + 
                     plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2, 1))) + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & 
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

p
ggsave(filename="./figures/figure3.png", p, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 1200)
```

## Figure 4

We evaluate the statistical power of the sLD test, assessing whether it has the ability to detect true instances of structural LD. As such, we implement the forward-generating probability model for genotype pairs in structural LD outlined in the manuscript (specifically in the Appendices). We first generate IAFs for $J = 800$ individuals at $I = 200000$ loci under an admixture model with $K=4$ admixed populations. Our simulation parameters and distributions closely mirror those used for [Figure 3](#sec-fig3), only we have a larger number of loci here. 

From these IAFs, we then draw genotypes -- some in structural LD, and others not in structural LD. Genotype pairs *not* in structural LD are essentially jointly independent binomial draws in accordance with the coancestry model. For genotype pairs in structural LD, we must tune the value of their individual-specific LD coefficient $\delta_{ab,j}$. Note that the possible values of $\delta_{ab,j}$ are constrained, as detailed in the manuscript, by $D_{\min}(\pi_{aj}, \pi_{bj})$ and $D_{\max}(\pi_{aj}, \pi_{bj})$ -- the minimum and maximum possible values of the LD coefficient given two allele frequencies $\pi_{aj}$ and $\pi_{bj}$. These constraints ensure that haplotype frequencies under our framework are non-negative values summing up to one. Thus, given $\pi_{aj}$ and $\pi_{bj}$, and assuming positive LD, we first compute $D_{\max}(\pi_{aj}, \pi_{bj})$ and then set 
$$
\delta_{ab,j} = \min\{\rho_{ab} \sqrt{\pi_{aj}(1-\pi_{aj})\pi_{bj}(1-\pi_{bj})}, D_{\max}(\pi_{aj}, \pi_{bj})\},
$$
where $\rho_{ab}$ denotes some (non-negative) target conditional correlation. In our simulations, we chose a range of $\rho_{ab}$ from $0.1$ to $0.5$ in increments of $0.05$. Note that for a given value of $\rho_{ab}$ in this analysis, all non-null pairs have that value of $\rho_{ab}$ set as the target conditional correlation so that the signal of structural LD is consistent within a given simulation replicate. We conduct 300 simulation replicates for each value of $\rho_{ab}$. 

### Draw IAFs

```{r, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(999)
J_ind <- 800
I_loci <- 200000
K_subpops <- 4

# Draw admixture model parameters
inbr_subpops <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4)
admix_proportions <- bnpsd::admix_prop_1d_linear(J_ind, K_subpops, sigma = 1)

# Draw IAFs
p_anc <- bnpsd::draw_p_anc(I_loci, p_min = 0.05, p_max = 0.95)
p_subpops <- bnpsd::draw_p_subpops(p_anc, inbr_subpops)
p_ind <- bnpsd::make_p_ind_admix(p_subpops, admix_proportions)
p_ind[p_ind < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind) # truncate small/large IAFs
p_ind[p_ind > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)

min_MAF <- 0.05 # Minimum MAF filter if desired
# p_ind <- p_ind[rowMeans(p_ind) >= min_MAF & 
# rowMeans(p_ind) <= (1 - min_MAF), ]
m_kept <- nrow(p_ind)
```

### Perform sLD test on simulated null and non-null pairs

We provide a function $\texttt{sim\_mat\_with\_haplo()}$ that generates a genotype matrix in which certain pairs of genotypes (for a given individual) are in structural LD. The helper function $\texttt{run\_single\_simulation()}$ in turn runs one instance of our statistical power simulations, while $\texttt{compute\_FDR\_power()}$ calculates the false discovery rate (FDR) and statistical power given a set of $p$-values, the indices corresponding to the true alternate hypotheses among these $p$-values, and a threshold for $q$-values. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
compute_FDR_power <- function(p_val_vec, alt_ids, q_threshold) {
  
  q_val_vec <- qvalue(p_val_vec, pi0 = 1)
  rejected <- which(q_val_vec$qvalues <= q_threshold)
  FDR <- if (length(rejected) > 0) 
    length(setdiff(rejected, alt_ids)) / length(rejected) 
  else 0
  power <- length(intersect(rejected, alt_ids)) / length(alt_ids)
  
  return(c(FDR, power))
}

# m_kept can be adjusted if any filtering is done on minimum MAF
run_single_simulation <- function(s, p_ind, rho, q_threshold = 0.1, 
                                  m_kept = nrow(p_ind)) {
  
  # Generate genotypes
  pair_ids <- matrix(1:5000, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) # indices of non-null SNP pairs
  n_null_pairs <- 5e4 # number of null hypotheses
  alt_ids <- 1:2500 # indices of non-null p-values
  
  X <- sim_mat_with_haplo(p_ind, pair_ids, rho = rho)
  
  full_pairlist <- rbind(
    pair_ids,
    t(replicate(n_null_pairs, sample(5001:m_kept, 2)))
  )
  n_pairs <- nrow(full_pairlist)

  # Estimate and truncate IAFs
  p_hat <- estimate_F(X, d = 4)$F_hat
  J_ind <- ncol(p_hat)
  p_hat[p_hat < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind)
  p_hat[p_hat > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)
  
  p_trad <- matrix(
    rowMeans(X/2, na.rm = TRUE),
    nrow = nrow(X), 
    ncol = ncol(X)
  )
  p_trad[p_trad < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind)
  p_trad[p_trad > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)

  test_stat_theor_vec <- numeric(n_pairs)
  test_stat_imp_vec <- numeric(n_pairs)
  test_stat_trad_vec <- numeric(n_pairs)

  for (i in 1:n_pairs) {
    locus_a <- full_pairlist[i, 1]
    locus_b <- full_pairlist[i, 2]
    X_a <- X[locus_a, ]
    X_b <- X[locus_b, ]
    
    test_stat_theor_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_a, X_b, p_ind[locus_a, ], p_ind[locus_b, ])
    test_stat_imp_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_a, X_b, p_hat[locus_a, ], p_hat[locus_b, ])
    test_stat_trad_vec[i] <- sLD_SNP(X_a, X_b, p_trad[locus_a, ], p_trad[locus_b, ])
  }
  
  # Compute p-values 
  p_val_theor_vec <- compute_p_val(test_stat_theor_vec)
  p_val_imp_vec <- compute_p_val(test_stat_imp_vec)
  p_val_trad_vec <- compute_p_val(test_stat_trad_vec)
  
  # Compute FDR and power metrics
  out_theor <- compute_FDR_power(p_val_theor_vec, alt_ids, q_threshold = q_threshold)
  out_imp <- compute_FDR_power(p_val_imp_vec, alt_ids, q_threshold = q_threshold)
  out_trad <- compute_FDR_power(p_val_trad_vec, alt_ids, q_threshold = q_threshold)
  
  return(list(theor = out_theor, imp = out_imp, naive = out_trad))
}
```

We include a representative example of running a set of simulation replicates for a given value of $\rho$ (0.5 in this case). We ran these simulations on the ARGO cluster to speed up compute time; the directory $\texttt{./rdata/power\_sim}$ contains the output of these simulations. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(42)
n_simulation <- 300
rho <- 0.5

FDR_theor_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)
power_theor_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)
FDR_imp_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)
power_imp_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)
FDR_trad_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)
power_trad_vec <- numeric(n_simulation)

# Using p_ind we draw previously 
for (s in 1:n_simulation) {
    sim_res <- run_single_simulation(s, p_ind = p_ind, rho = rho)
    
    FDR_theor_vec[s] <- sim_res$theor[1]
    power_theor_vec[s] <- sim_res$theor[2]
    
    FDR_imp_vec[s] <- sim_res$imp[1]
    power_imp_vec[s] <- sim_res$imp[2]
    
    FDR_trad_vec[s] <- sim_res$naive[1]
    power_trad_vec[s] <- sim_res$naive[2]
}

saveRDS(FDR_theor_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/fdr_theor_0.5.rds")
saveRDS(power_theor_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/power_theor_0.5.rds")
saveRDS(FDR_imp_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/fdr_imp_0.5.rds")
saveRDS(power_imp_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/power_imp_0.5.rds")
saveRDS(FDR_trad_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/fdr_trad_0.5.rds")
saveRDS(power_trad_vec, file = "./rdata/power_sim/power_trad_0.5.rds")
```

## Figure 5

Our workflow for this figure closely mirrors that of @sec-fig1, in that we randomly draw interchromosomal locus pairs and perform the sLD test for these pairs. This process is already documented for the TGP in @sec-fig1 so we will only show the steps for the HGDP and the HO study below. However, we will demonstrate, using the TGP, an approach for a researcher to choose the number of admixed populations $K$ in an estimated model of population structure.

### Procedure for selecting $K$ 

We briefly describe our procedure for choosing the number of admixed populations $K$ in an admixture model of population structure, which closely follows an algorithm introduced for the related sHWE test [@hao2019]. We analyze the TGP in this example. Specifically, for each value of $K$, we compute the (Shannon) entropy of its corresponding $p$-value distribution (these are $p$-values computed for interchromosomal locus pairs). This process begins with partitioning the interval $[0,1]$ into $B$ equally sized bins. We then compute the entropy, defined as $-\sum_{b=1}^B f_b \log_2(f_b)$, where $f_b$ is the proportion of $p$-values falling into the $b$th bin. We can choose the value of $K$ corresponding to the largest entropy value, at the start of a plateau in entropy values, or via some other metric. In our analyses, we select the smallest value of $K$ within an entropy plateau such that its corresponding histogram of $p$-values is qualitatively close to the $\text{Uniform}(0,1)$ distribution. 

```{r, eval=TRUE}
entropy_vec <- numeric()
id_vec <- c(1:24)

for (i in id_vec) {
  obs_ts <- sprintf("./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_K%s_diff_chr.rds", i)
  obs_ts <- readRDS(obs_ts)
  p_k <- compute_p_val(obs_ts)
  entropy_vec <- c(entropy_vec, compute_entropy(p_k, n_bin = 20))
}

plot(id_vec, entropy_vec, main = "TGP: Entropy vs. K", type = "l",
     xlab = "K", ylab = "Entropy")
```

## Figure 6

This figure plots sLD test $p$-values for pairs of loci residing on the same chromosome. We will use the same SNP annotations (BioMart) from the preceding figures to determine which chromosome each SNP falls on. The two helper functions below are used to facilitate the sampling of locus pairs within a given chromosome. The first function, $\texttt{sample\_snp\_pairs\_by\_distance()}$, samples pairs of SNPs on a given chromosome within a physical distance (in base pairs) window $[\texttt{lower\_bound}, \texttt{upper\_bound}]$. The second function, $\texttt{sample\_window\_across\_chr()}$, applies $\texttt{sample\_snp\_pairs\_by\_distance()}$ to each of the 22 autosomes. 

We would then carry out the sLD test using the function $\texttt{sLD()}$, inputting the corresponding pairs of indices as argument (see above for sample implementations).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Helper functions for sampling locus pairs on a given chromosome
sample_snp_pairs_by_distance <- function(positions, rsids, lower_bound, upper_bound, 
                                         n_pairs = 1000, max_trials = 5e3) {
  n <- length(positions)
  pairs <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = n_pairs, ncol = 2)
  bp_distance <- numeric(n_pairs)
  count <- 0
  trials <- 0

  while (count < n_pairs && trials < max_trials) {
    i <- sample.int(n - 1, 1)
    pos_i <- positions[i]
    rel_dist <- positions[(i+1):n] - pos_i
    valid_j_rel <- which(rel_dist >= lower_bound & rel_dist <= upper_bound)

    if (length(valid_j_rel) > 0) {
      if (length(valid_j_rel) == 1) {
        j <- i + valid_j_rel
      } else {
        j <- i + sample(valid_j_rel, 1)
      }
      count <- count + 1
      pairs[count, ] <- c(rsids[i], rsids[j])
      bp_distance[count] <- abs(pos_i - positions[j])
    }
    trials <- trials + 1
  }

  if (count < n_pairs) {
    pairs <- pairs[1:count, , drop = FALSE]
    warning(sprintf("Only %d pairs found (target was %d)", count, n_pairs))
  }

  return(list(pairs = pairs, bp_distance = bp_distance))
}

sample_window_across_chr <- function(snp_df, lower_bound, upper_bound, 
                                    n_pairs_per_chr = 1000, 
                                    max_trials = n_pairs_per_chr*10) {
  
  window_ids <- matrix(nrow = 22*n_pairs_per_chr, ncol=2)
  window_distance <- numeric(22*n_pairs_per_chr)
  
  for (i in 1:22) {
    chr_df <- snp_df[snp_df$chr_name == i,]
    chr_df <- chr_df[order(chr_df$chrom_start, decreasing=F),]
    sampleid <- sample_snp_pairs_by_distance(chr_df$chrom_start, chr_df$refsnp_id,
                                             n_pairs = n_pairs_per_chr,
                                             max_trials = max_trials,
                                             lower_bound = lower_bound, 
                                             upper_bound = upper_bound)
    window_distance[((i-1)*n_pairs_per_chr+1):(i*n_pairs_per_chr)] <- sampleid$bp_distance
    window_ids[((i-1)*n_pairs_per_chr+1):(i*n_pairs_per_chr), ] <- sampleid$pairs
  }
  
  return(list(pairs = window_ids, bp_distance = window_distance))
}
```

### Sample locus pairs for the TGP

We will first sample locus pairs for the TGP. Recall that $\texttt{snp\_info\_TGP}$ contains annotations for most of the SNPs in the TGP dataset. We sample locus pairs belonging to four base pair distance windows: $0$ to $5$ kbp, $5$ to $50$ kbp, $50$ to $500$ kbp, and $500$ kbp to $5$ Mbp. We store (base pair) distances between pairs of loci and locus pair indices within the directory $\texttt{./rdata/TGP\_rdata/same\_chr}$.

### Code for plotting 

We introduce a helper function $\texttt{make\_binned\_df()}$ to generate a dataframe for plotting. We group $-\log_{10}(p$-values) into bins based on the physical distance between loci (within a given pair), then calculate the mean within these bins. 

```{r}
make_binned_df <- function(p_vec, distances) {
  
  x <- distances
  y <- -log10(p_vec)
  y <- pmin(y, 16) # truncate p-values 
  df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
  
  # Create bins and compute mean per bin 
  bin_width <- 0.25
  df_binned <- df %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(x, breaks = seq(0, 7, by = bin_width), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarize(
      mean_x = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_y = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE, trim=0.05),
      var_x = var(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_y = var(y, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
    
  return(df_binned)
}
```

## Figure 7

### Obtain locus pairs spanning the HLA region

We first identify SNPs mapping to the HLA region, which resides on Chromosome 6; we obtained coordinates for this region from [@kulski2022]. We restrict our analyses to an approximately 1 Mb window in this region, and halve the number of SNPs for computational feasibility and plotting. 

Like before, we can carry out the sLD test once we identify a set of locus pairs. Here, these pair indices are contained within $\texttt{HLA\_TGP\_indices.rds}$. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
hla_mapping <- snp_info_TGP %>%
  filter(chr_name == 6, 
         chrom_start >= 32400000, 
         chrom_start <= 33400000) %>%
  arrange(chrom_start)

thin_factor <- 2
hla_rsid_thinned <- hla_mapping$refsnp_id[seq(1, nrow(hla_mapping), by = thin_factor)]
pairs_matrix <- combn(hla_rsid_thinned, 2)
TGP_HLA_ids <- match_rsid_index(pairs_matrix, rsid_TGP)
saveRDS(TGP_HLA_ids, file="./rdata/TGP_rdata/HLA_TGP_indices.rds")
saveRDS(pairs_matrix, file="./rdata/TGP_rdata/HLA_TGP_coordinates.rds")
```

### Code for plotting 

```{r, eval=TRUE}
make_heatmap_df <- function(pairs_df) {
  
  plot_df <- pairs_df %>%
    left_join(snp_info_TGP, by = c("snpa" = "refsnp_id")) %>%
    rename(pos_a = chrom_start) %>%
    left_join(snp_info_TGP, by = c("snpb" = "refsnp_id")) %>%
    rename(pos_b = chrom_start)
  plot_df_rotated <- plot_df %>%
    mutate(x_coord = (pos_a + pos_b) / 2, # horizontal center between two SNP
           y_coord = abs(pos_a - pos_b) / 2) # height represents how far apart they are
  
  return(plot_df_rotated)
}
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
logp_K1 <- pmin(logp_K1, 16)

                       value = logp_K1)
plot_df_trad <- make_heatmap_df(pairs_df)
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
pairs_df <- data.frame(snpa = HLA_coords[1, ], snpb = HLA_coords[2, ], 
                       value = logp_K12)
plot_df_sLD <- make_heatmap_df(pairs_df)
```

## Figure 11 {#sec-fig11}

We evaluate the fit of the $\text{Normal}(0,1)$ theoretical null distribution for the TGP by comparing it to an empirical null distribution (generated via the parametric bootstrap approach detailed in [@hao2019]). From our simulated genotypes, we carry out a total of $2 \times 10^6$ hypothesis tests, resulting in $2 \times 10^6$ null test statistics. In order to see whether the empirical null distribution is approximately $\text{Normal}(0,1)$ distributed, we compute two-sided $p$-values from our empirical test statistics using the $\text{Normal}(0,1)$ cumulative distribution function (CDF). If the empirical null distribution is roughly $\text{Normal}(0,1)$, we would expect to see a  $\text{Uniform}(0,1)$ distribution of $p$-values. We compute the two-sided $p$-value $2(1-\Phi(\lvert T^{(J)}_{ab}(\hat{\mathbf{\Pi}}^0_{ab})\rvert))$ for each test statistic $T^{(J)}_{ab}(\hat{\mathbf{\Pi}}^0_{ab})$, where $\Phi(\cdot)$ denotes the $\text{Normal}(0,1)$ CDF. To better visualize tail behavior, we chose to plot a quantile-quantile plot of $p$-values against theoretical uniform quantiles on a logarithmic axis, rather than comparing test statistic directly against $\text{Normal}(0,1)$ quantiles. We perform this analysis for a wide range of admixed population counts $K$. 

### Simulate empirical null 

We include a sample implementation (using a population model with $K=3$ admixed populations) for simulating an empirical null distribution of test statistics. Note that we performed this analysis, like several of the previous analyses, on the ARGO cluster. We store null test statistics in the directory $\texttt{./rdata/TGP\_rdata/null\_stats}$.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Convert BEDmatrix to R matrix 
X_TGP <- t(as.matrix(TGP)) # transpose to get loci x individuals format
X_TGP <- alstructure:::impute_mean(X_TGP) # impute missing values in genotype matrix

# Estimate IAFs
K <- 3 # choose the number of admixed populations
TGP_Pi_hat <- alstructure::estimate_F(X_TGP, d = K)$F_hat # estimated IAFs

# Draw null genotypes, re-estimate IAFs
X_0_TGP <- draw_genotypes_admix(TGP_Pi_hat)
Pi_hat_0_TGP <- alstructure::estimate_F(X_0_TGP, d = K)$F_hat

# Run sLD
TGP_diff_chr_ids <- readRDS("./rdata/TGP_rdata/diff_chr/TGP_diff_chr_ids.rds") 
J_ind <- ncol(X_0_TGP) 
Pi_hat_0_TGP[Pi_hat_0_TGP < 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1/(2*J_ind) # truncate IAF estimates 
Pi_hat_0_TGP[Pi_hat_0_TGP > 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)] <- 1 - 1/(2*J_ind)
TGP_test_stats_null_K3 <- sLD(X_0_TGP, Pi_hat_0_TGP, TGP_diff_chr_ids)
saveRDS(TGP_test_stats_null_K3, 
        file = "./rdata/TGP_rdata/null_stats/TGP_K3_null_stats.rds")
```

### Code for plotting

Because we analyzed a large number of $p$-values, we chose to sample a subset of them for each quantile-quantile plot to avoid a prohibitively large file size for the final figure. We restrict this downsampling to larger $p$-values, keeping all $p$-values $< 0.01$ to preserve the tail behavior of our empirical distribution. We include a function below, $\texttt{downsample\_indices()}$, that carries out this downsampling procedure; the argument $\texttt{sample\_size}$ denotes the target number of $p$-values to keep. Note that we apply this downsampling to both the observed $p$-values as well as the paired theoretical $\text{Uniform}(0,1)$ quantiles. 

```{r, eval=TRUE}
downsample_indices <- function(test_stats, sample_size=2e4) {
  
  # Sort test statistics in decreasing order (i.e., increasing p-values)
  n_total <- length(test_stats)
  abs_ts_sorted <- sort(abs(test_stats), decreasing = TRUE)
  p_sorted <- compute_p_val(abs_ts_sorted)
  p_theo_all <- ppoints(length(test_stats))
  
  # Keep all small p-values
  tail_indices <- which(p_sorted < 0.01) 
  if (length(tail_indices) > 0) {
    tail_limit <- max(tail_indices)
    tail_idx <- 1:tail_limit
  } else {
    tail_limit <- 0
    tail_idx <- integer(0)
  }
  
  # Downsample the "bulk" region containing larger p-values
  if (tail_limit < n_total) {
    bulk_start <- tail_limit + 1
    n_bulk <- n_total - bulk_start + 1
    if (n_bulk > sample_size) {
      bulk_idx <- unique(round(seq(bulk_start, n_total, length.out = sample_size)))
    } else {
      bulk_idx <- bulk_start:n_total
    }
  } else {
    bulk_idx <- integer(0)
  }
  
  keep_idx <- c(tail_idx, bulk_idx)
  return(list(obs = p_sorted[keep_idx], 
              theo = p_theo_all[keep_idx]))
}
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
p_vec <- c()
theo_vec <- c()
id_vec <- c()

for (i in 2:25) {
  file_path <- sprintf(
    "./rdata/TGP_rdata/null_stats/TGP_K%s_null_stats.rds", i
  )
  obs_ts <- readRDS(file_path)
  downsampled_p <- downsample_indices(obs_ts)
  p_vec <- c(p_vec, downsampled_p$obs)
  theo_vec <- c(theo_vec, downsampled_p$theo)
  id_vec <- c(id_vec, rep(i, length(downsampled_p$theo)))
}

sLD_df_TGP_null <- data.frame(id = id_vec, sample = -log10(p_vec), theo = -log10(theo_vec))
sLD_df_TGP_null$id <- as.factor(sLD_df_TGP_null$id)
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.2) + 
  facet_wrap(~id, labeller=as_labeller(labels,
             default=label_parsed), ncol=4) + theme_bw() +
  theme(text=element_text(family="sans", size=10),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=8),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.5,"lines"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6),
        aspect.ratio = 0.7,
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6, margin = 
                                    margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = 1, l = 1)),
        strip.background = element_blank()) +
```
